thread.title: Browns continue Thursday night win streak with 27-24 victory over Steelers
thread.title_full: Browns continue Thursday night win streak with 27-24 victory over Steelers

author: WEWS
title: Browns continue Thursday night win streak with 27-24 victory over Steelers
text:
The Browns currently sit atop the AFC North after their 27-24 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers on Thursday.
CLEVELAND — The Browns currently sit atop the AFC North after their 27-24 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers on Thursday. The Browns record improved to 3-1 following a successful two-game home stand.
#Browns beat the Steelers, 27-24. Cleveland is now 3-1 on the season. What a win. pic.twitter.com/KJbYfaaoGu — Camryn Justice October 2, 2026 After a quick three-and-out drive to start the game, quarterback Deshaun Watson helped spark the Browns' offense. Rookie wide receivers Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion each made big downfield plays for significant gains.
Boston recorded four catches for 89 yards while Concepcion caught five for 65 yards. The first Browns touchdown of the night was scored by running back Jaleel McLaughlin on a 28 yard run. Ahead of the Thursday night matchup, McLaughlin spoke with News 5's Camryn Justice in a one-on-one interview for"Next Man Up.
" Watch related coverage: Get to know Browns RB Jaleel McLaughlin Next Man Up: Browns RB Jaleel McLaughlin has local football roots, enjoys working out and singing some Adele The Browns offense scored three touchdowns and recorded 372 total yards, including 112 rushing yards and 260 passing yards. Watson completed 24 of 33 passes with one interception and one fumble. The Steelers tied the game at 24-24 late in the fourth quarter with a touchdown and a successful two-point conversion.
The extra two points were made easier after an offsides penalty was called on defensive end Jared Verse. Watch previous coverage: Browns excited for primetime rivalry game against Steelers on Thursday 'It's huge, it's major': Browns excited for primetime rivalry game against Steelers on Thursday However, the Browns' offensive unit was able to march back down the field to allow kicker Andre Szmyt to score the game-winning field goal with 10 seconds remaining.
The kick was made from 56 yards out, the longest of his NFL career. Afterwards, Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers had a final chance to get the Steelers in field goal range, but he was picked off by Grant Delpit at the Browns 18 yard-line with 1 second left. Earlier in the game, the Browns' defensive unit did lose a major player during the primetime matchup.
In the first quarter of Thursday's game, defensive tackle Mason Graham went down on the field after it appeared his leg bent awkwardly. After being checked by trainers, Graham limped off the field and into the blue medical tent for observation before heading to the locker room for further evaluation. Coming out of the half, Graham was officially ruled out for the remainder of the game.
With Graham sidelined, the Browns turned to Mike Hall Jr. to step in at defensive tackle, who also sustained an injury a short time later. However, Hall would return to the game during the second half and record a major sack against Rodgers. Cleveland’s defense sacked Rodgers a total of five times. The 3-1 Browns will travel to MetLife Stadium to face off against the New York Jets on Oct. 11.
